title: README and project documentation
learningObjectives: Complete readme and project documentation using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: Project documentation should explain purpose, setup, dependencies, scripts, structure, configuration, testing, deployment, and known limitations. Documentation must match the current implementation and must not contain credentials or private data.
understand.whyItMatters: Accurate documentation reduces onboarding time and prevents unsafe setup assumptions. Update documentation alongside changes that affect how the project is used.
understand.analogy: Documentation is the map that lets another developer find the entrance, tools, and safe route through a project.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The outline covers key information for a contributor. Every command should be checked against the actual project.

examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Write a README for the capstone and verify every setup command, script, path, and deployment note against the repository.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
